jobs.title: Solutions Engineer, Public Sector
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Domino, we build software that helps the largest, AI-driven organizations build and operate advanced data science and AI solutions at scale. Our platform integrates a streamlined model development environment, MLOps capabilities, and novel features for collaboration, reuse, and reproducibility — all of which make data science teams more productive, reduce time to value, and ensure compliance. Our customers — like Johnson & Johnson, GSK, Bristol Myers, UBS, FINRA and the US Navy — are using our software to solve some of the most important challenges in the world, such as developing new medicines, securing our financial markets, or protecting our country. Backed by Sequoia Capital, Coatue Management, NVIDIA, Snowflake and other leading investors, we have been in business for a decade but are still a small team operating with the spirit of a startup. Especially in the world of AI today, we believe that the future is still being invented — and we want to be the ones building it. For more information, visit www.domino.ai

What We Are Building

Our Sales Engineering team is at the heart of transforming curiosity into confidence. We help prospects envision the full potential of our platform, guiding them from discovery to realization. Working closely with Enterprise Account Executives, our Sales Engineers craft compelling product demonstrations, design and execute impactful proof-of-concepts, and shape technical strategies that drive successful customer implementations.

As a growing company, our Sales Engineers play a pivotal role beyond just sales—collaborating across Marketing, Product Management, and Engineering to bridge the gap between market needs and product innovation. If you thrive in an environment where your technical expertise fuels real business impact, and where your insights help shape the future of our platform, you’ll feel right at home here.

What Your Impact Will Be

Lead technical evaluations and demonstrations of the Domino platform for customers across the Department of Defense, civilian agencies, federally funded research and development centers (FFRDCs), and major defense contractors.
Design and execute proof-of-concept deployments tailored to each customer’s environment and mission needs, showcasing Domino’s integration with their data science workflows and infrastructure.
Collaborate with account executives to craft solution architectures that meet federal security and compliance standards (e.g., FedRAMP, IL5).
Develop and maintain reusable demonstration environments and technical assets that accelerate future sales cycles.
Drive post-POC adoption readiness by partnering with Customer Success and Solutions Architects to ensure a smooth handoff into deployment.
Success will be evident through higher technical win rates, reduced time to close, and increased adoption within key government accounts.

What We Look For In This Role

Security Clearance: This position requires an active U.S. Secret Security Clearance (US Citizenship required), with the ability to obtain a Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) Security Clearance and program access (post start). A U.S. Security Clearance that has been active in the past 24 months is considered active.
Proven success in pre-sales or solutions engineering, ideally supporting enterprise software or AI/ML platforms. This does not necessarily need to be at a software vendor, equivalent solution engineering tasks internally or as a consultant developer could work.
Experience with U.S. public sector customers, especially within federal agencies, defense, or national labs — understanding their procurement processes, compliance constraints, and security environments.
Track record of leading successful technical evaluations or pilots that resulted in multimillion-dollar enterprise or government software deals.
Experience working in complex, highly regulated IT environments, including hybrid or air-gapped systems.
Proficiency in Python, R, and modern data science / machine learning tools.
Familiarity with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), cloud platforms (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, GCP), and networking concepts.
Understanding of the end-to-end AI lifecycle, from experimentation to production.

What We Value

We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply
We value a growth mindset. High-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and see the opportunities for success
We believe in individuals who seek truth and speak the truth and can be their whole selves at work
We value all of you that believe improving is always possible. At Domino, everything is a work in progress – we can do better at everything
We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate's experience, qualifications, and location. Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

Total Compensation Range

$200,000—$250,000 USD

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Optum is a global organization that delivers care, aided by technology to help millions of people live healthier lives. The work you do with our team will directly improve health outcomes by connecting people with the care, pharmacy benefits, and data they need to feel their best. Here, you will find a culture guided by diversity and inclusion, talented peers, comprehensive benefits, and career development opportunities. Come make an impact on the communities we serve as you help us advance health equity on a global scale. Join us to start  Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

You will enjoy the flexibility to telecommute* from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges.

Primary Responsibilities

Works with the implementation architect and sales teams to assess internal or potential data assets, and identify high level gaps or risks
Performs high level layout gap analysis as well as deep dive implementation analysis for a wide variety of use cases
Leads client data education and data resolution calls and working sessions
Coordinates DUR and/or De-ID submittals and approvals
Manages data acquisition, file inventory, and file transfer process from asset owners to appropriate pipeline location (SFTP ownership and management)
Works with client and internal product teams to determine client specific reporting and operational needs and assists in new product readiness
Provides representation and communication on status calls to clients
Provides in depth mapping, data validation/QC requirements, and manually validates when needed. Tracks all issues in a data IRAD
Coordinates with downstream teams to resolve data questions and issues
Provides ongoing support for data issues that requires communication with the client (Tier 3 prod support)
Responsible for coordinating alignment of pre-pay and post-pay data sets when needed (shared reference fields)
Mature the organization by creating and improving process artifacts as well as communication and gaining support for the process models across many teams
Leads and fully documents 'as-is' and 'to-be' business process states. Recognize gaps between current situation and desired outcome and utilize appropriate resources to obtain information, consider options and deliver the appropriate solution to mitigate gaps

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree
5+ years of SQL experience querying complex datasets
5+ years of experience in managed healthcare
5+ years of structured data mapping experience
3+ years of experience in an external client-facing role
2+ years of experience working in agile environment
2+ years of experience with Azure DataBricks

Preferred Qualifications

Able to gather requirements and translate business requirements to technical requirements
Strong communication skills
All Telecommuters will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group's Telecommuter Policy.

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The hourly pay for this role will range from $91,700 to $163,700 per hour based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Application Deadline:
This will be posted for a minimum of 2 business days or until a sufficient candidate pool has been collected. Job posting may come down early due to volume of applicants.

At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and make the health system work better for everyone. We believe everyone-of every race, gender, sexuality, age, location, and income-deserves the opportunity to live their healthiest life. Today, however, there are still far too many barriers to good health which are disproportionately experienced by people of color, historically marginalized groups, and those with lower incomes. We are committed to mitigating our impact on the environment and enabling and delivering equitable care that addresses health disparities and improves health outcomes - an enterprise priority reflected in our mission.

Job Description

The Division of Medical Physics in the Department of Radiation Oncology is seeking a Residency Program Coordinator 2, to manage, administer and support the operations of the Medical Physics residency program, postdoctoral scholars and visiting students. The Stanford Medical Physics residency program is accredited by the CAMPEP -- Commission on Accreditation of Medical Physics Education Programs.

The Division of Medical Physics core values are based on professionalism, integrity, and service. Our culture promotes, recognizes, and values the role of staff as partners in an environment that attracts and fosters the highest quality.

Desired Qualifications

In-depth knowledge and understanding of administrative principles and practices, as well as ability to assimilate functional operating knowledge of Stanford University.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:

Constantly perform desk-based computer tasks.
Frequently sitting.
Occasionally stand/walk, reach/work above shoulders, grasp lightly/fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, use a telephone, sort/file paperwork or parts, lift/carry/push/pull objects that weigh up to 10 pounds.
Rarely twist/bend/stoop/squat, kneel/crawl.
- Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of his or her job.

Work Standards

Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations.
Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned.
Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University's Administrative Guide, http://adminguide.stanford.edu .

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Independently implement, administer and evaluate day-to-day activities of residency/clinical fellowship program(s) by identifying and executing responsibilities, making recommendations that impact policies, programs and standards, and ensuring compliance and follow-up, as needed.
Act as key contact for the program to interpret and apply complex policies, procedures and program guidelines (such as those from ACGME – Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education). Review exceptions to policies to determine if exceptions are allowable. Identify, troubleshoot and report compliance issues and assist in correcting situations.
Initiate and manage the annual recruitment, onboarding and offboarding processes, including coordinating all interviews and collecting feedback on applicants. Summarize ratings and provide recommendations to program director and selection committee.
Participate in ranking meetings and provide feedback on strengths/suitability of applicants. Communicate requirements to newly matched residents. Administer appointments to the hospitals/university.
Manage the residency/clinical fellowship and faculty evaluation process by establishing and executing project plans, timelines, and objectives. Present analysis of programs and evaluations.
Develop, distribute, maintain and analyze the resident rotation, vacation and leave schedules based on accreditation requirements with oversight of Program Director.
Ensure compliance with accreditation, licensing board, professional association, ACGME requirements, GME Office requirements for the residency curriculum, goals and objectives for each level of training. Ensure interns are credentialed before starting any rotation.
Act as a liaison and advocate in support of residents and hospital administration. Establish relationships and act as a liaison to other hospitals, internal departments, and divisions regarding resident recruitment, orientation, annual program affiliation agreements, and external rotations. Manage the goals and objectives for fellows’ rotations through other clinics; recommend actions to be taken if goals are not being met.
May assist with budget activities for various residency activities, including monitoring expenses.
Plan annual events, organize meetings, and assist in the preparation for ACGME Site Visits and internal reviews. Develop brochures, invitations, or advertisements for events/lectures.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree and two years of relevant experience, or combination of education and relevant experience.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Ability to work independently and to coordinate multiple assignments with fluctuating priorities.
Excellent organizational and analytical abilities, ability to handle diverse workload.
Demonstrated good judgment in all areas of responsibility.
Agile and quick learner who can adapt easily to Stanford specific software and clinically related software.
Demonstrated ability to work well independently and take initiative while problem solving and resolving challenges.
Excellent oral and written communication skills. Ability to work with all levels of faculty and staff, and exhibit significant degree of diplomacy.
Excellent customer service skills and ability to adapt to changing work environment.
Proficient with Excel, Word and other applications required.
Ability to learn, understand and apply Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or other subspecialties guidelines.

With subsidiaries located in California, Missouri, Canada, UK, India, and China, companies around the world depend on HME for clear, reliable communication solutions. From setting the standard for drive-thru headsets and timer systems in the quick service restaurant (QSR) industry to developing professional audio equipment used in the Olympic Games, HME strives to create the newest, most innovative products on the market while providing quality care and attention to its customers. We are currently hiring for an Associate Project Coordinator
on 2nd Shift (start time between 5-8PM and end time between 1:30-4:30AM).

jobs.title: Program Coordinator for Adult Day Program
jobs.description:
At Dungarvin, we are dedicated to making a meaningful impact in the lives of individuals with diverse abilities. We provide essential support to those with intellectual and developmental disabilities, physical disabilities, autism, and mental health conditions - empowering them to thrive in their communities. Where barriers exist, we create pathways for inclusion and independence.

About our Adult Day Program:

Our Adult Day Program provides structured daytime services for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Individuals participate in skill-building, recreational, educational, and community-based activities that support independence, social connection, and personal goals. Staff work directly with individuals throughout the day, providing instruction, encouragement, personal care, behavioral support, and opportunities for meaningful participation.

The Role:

We are looking for an organized, confident, and proactive Program Coordinator for our Adult Day Program in Long Beach, CA.

The Program Coordinator (PC) is the lead Direct Support Professional (DSP) within the program. This is a hands-on working lead role, not a traditional administrative or supervisory position.

The PC works directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities throughout the day, providing personal care, instruction, skill development, and positive behavioral support. The goal is simple: keep individuals safe, engaged, supported, and moving toward greater independence.

The PC also helps keep the program running. This includes coordinating daily activities, adjusting schedules, supporting documentation, reinforcing expectations, and providing day-to-day guidance to DSP staff. The PC reports to the Program Director and leads through communication, consistency, and example, without formal supervisory authority.

Why You’ll Love This Role:

Competitive Pay:
$23.75/hour
Full Range Scale
: $23.75 - $26.45 per hour ( The starting rate for this position is fixed at $23.75 per hour. Pay increases occur over time and are tied to tenure/length of employment with Dungarvin.)
Meaningful Work:
Help individuals build skills, independence, and community connections
Leadership Opportunities:
Lead by example while coaching, guiding, and supporting staff
Variety:
Balance direct support, daily scheduling, staff guidance, communication, and program coordination.
Community Connections:
Help build partnerships and foster a vibrant, inclusive program environment.
Professional Growth:
Develop leadership, communication, documentation, and program coordination skills while continuing to work directly with the people we support.

Benefits & Perks:

Full Time Monday-Friday, daytime hours

training and orientation

Job Description

The Program Coordinator provides direct support to individuals while helping coordinate the daily flow of the Adult Day Program and ensuring staff are supported and aligned.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Provide hands-on direct support to adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
Assist individuals with personal care, hygiene, mobility, meals, communication, community participation, and other daily needs.
Model and implement behavior supports, including de-escalation techniques during challenging situations
Support individuals in achieving personal goals and increasing independence
Lead by example and provide day-to-day guidance, coaching, and support to DSP staff
Complete accurate and timely progress notes, reports, data tracking, and other required documentation
Assist with individual goals, ISP updates, and documentation expectations
Assist with basic program operations; coordinate transportation, community activities, program supplies, and other daily operational needs
Communicate professionally and effectively with families, providers, and interdisciplinary teams
Follow established health, safety, licensing, medication, transportation, and program procedures
Communicate concerns, changes, or operational challenges to the Program Director
Maintain the rights, dignity, health, safety, and confidentiality of the individuals served

Qualifications

Education & Experience:

Bachelors degree in Human Services, Special Education, or related field is preferred . Or, equivalent training/experience in disability services will be considered.
A minimum of one (1) year of experience supporting individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities is required.

At least one (1) year of experience in adult day program, vocational program, residential program, behavioral health setting, educational setting, or other community-based disability service

Skills & Abilities:

Confident and professional communicator
Able to clearly communicate information, concerns, expectations, and program updates
Able to lead, coach, and support peers without formal supervisory authority
Strong written communication and documentation skills
Organized and able to manage multiple responsibilities throughout the day
Ability to pivot when circumstances change
Calm, adaptable, creative, and solution-focused
Able to provide respectful, person-centered support
Comfortable working directly with individuals who may require personal care, behavioral support, mobility assistance, or physical assistance
Able to maintain professional relationships with individuals, staff, families, residential providers, Regional Center representatives, and other community partners
Tech savvy with computers, electronic documentation systems, email, spreadsheets, and other workplace technology
Able to work independently while recognizing when concerns must be communicated or elevated to the Program Director

Ability to lift and transfer 50 lbs.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At ERC Pathlight, we’re on a mission to change lives—and we’re looking for people who feel called to do the same.

As one of the nation’s leading treatment providers for eating disorders and mood, anxiety, and trauma-related conditions, we bring innovative, evidence-based, and deeply compassionate care to patients across the country. With multiple locations nationwide and extensive virtual programming, we meet patients exactly where they are and help them move toward lasting recovery.

Founded in 2008 by renowned psychiatrists and psychologists, ERC Pathlight now supports more than 6,000 patients each year. And as the need for world-class mental health care continues to rise, our commitment is stronger than ever: to expand access, elevate the standard of care, and empower every patient to rebuild their life with dignity and hope.

Why Join Us

When you join ERC Pathlight, you become part of a team that shows up every day to make a real difference. You’ll work alongside passionate clinicians, dedicated support staff, and mission-driven leaders who believe in collaboration, growth, and doing the right thing—always.

Here, your work matters. Your ideas matter. You
matter.

If you’re energized by purpose, motivated by impact, and ready to help transform the future of mental health treatment, you belong here.

Come build hope. Come save lives. Come grow with us.

Monday-Friday (8 hours shifts with some evenings until 715pm)

The Program Coordinator (PC I, PC II, PC III) is responsible for providing direct care and supervision to patients within inpatient, residential, and partial hospitalization levels of care at ERC Pathlight. Program Coordinators maintain a safe, structured, and therapeutic milieu while supporting the implementation of individualized treatment plans.

PCs provide patient supervision, maintain structure and boundaries, support therapeutic programming, assist with mealtime support, and complete required documentation. Level placement (I, II, III) is determined based on education, experience, and demonstrated competency.

Maintain daily program structure by following the established schedule
Complete observation rounds and safety checks as ordered by physician
Support patients with de-escalation and implementation of coping skills per treatment plan
Conduct room and luggage searches
Supervise fresh air breaks and mindful movement exposures
Provide ongoing bathroom monitoring
Obtain and document patient vital signs, weights, and urine specific gravity (as applicable by location/program)

Group Facilitation

Participate in facilitation of therapeutic groups
Complete required EHR documentation related to group facilitation
Support group-based social activities and meal outings

Meal Support

Complete timely and accurate meal-related documentation

As our Mountain Rescue Program Coordinator, you will be a vital asset to Flight for Life (FFL), directly supporting program leadership and crew as a dedicated subject matter expert in backcountry helicopter search and rescue (SAR) operations. Communicates protocols and procedures to the mountain rescue community, and represents Flight for Life on issues pertaining to backcountry helicopter SAR operations.

High School Diploma/G.E.D.

Helicopter SAR Operations experience
Valid Colorado driver's license and ability to pass the annual review of driving record for safe vehicle operations
Search and Rescue Technician or HEMS Certificate

*Preferred*

Prehospital experience

Proudly part of CommonSpirit Health, Flight For Life Colorado® was the first civilian, hospital-based emergency medical helicopter program in the United States. Automation mindset.

AI Nativity.

Modern data stack.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst / Modeler
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is seeking a GIS Analyst / Modeler
to join our Ocean Science team, with flexibility to be based in our South Kingstown, RI office, or work remotely within the Eastern or Central Region of the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For 60 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our science-based planning and design improves lives in our local communities and around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving  a lasting legacy .

Position Summary

We’re seeking a positive, motivated GIS Analyst / Modeler
with excellent problem-solving abilities and strong communication skills that will demonstrate an ability to work on highly dynamic and interactive projects both independently and as part of a team. This individual should have a strong technical background in GIS, data management, and a general understanding of, and interest in, environmental modeling. The successful candidate will be detail-oriented, working with a growing project team and offering GIS support for a variety of projects in inland, coastal, and offshore environments, ocean science, modeling, and data management.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Create, digitize, convert, edit, compile, and standardize GIS data from non-spatial sources.
Organize and structure spatial data files across servers and database environments, including maintaining data versioning as needed.
Perform QA/QC and data cleaning for geospatial, tabular, and model input/output data to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Research, gather, prepare, and integrate geospatial environmental data for use in modeling software.
Prepare and integrate gridded/raster and vector datasets from multiple sources for use as model inputs.
Use, enhance, and develop tools and workflows to analyze, interpret, and present model results.
Conduct modeling studies using proprietary model software.
Contribute to technical reports as an author or co-author.
Develop high-quality figures and maps for reports, presentations, and model documentation.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, engineering, computer science, oceanography, biology, environmental science, or a related scientific field.
A minimum of 1 year of relevant professional GIS experience, preferably in consulting, or 2 years of research-based GIS experience.
Proficiency with the Esri ArcGIS suite, including ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online, and extensions such as Spatial Analyst.
Familiarity with common GIS data formats, including geodatabases, shapefiles, and raster datasets.
Experience with GIS data creation, management, cleaning, and QA/QC.
Familiarity with cloud computing and working with hosted data.
Cartographic experience, including the design of maps for reports, web applications, posters, and other presentation materials.
Basic GIS programming/scripting experience in Python, including the ability to read, modify, and run existing scripts.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Access, Word, and PowerPoint.
Basic understanding of AI prompt engineering and agentic AI concepts to support workflow optimization.
Strong problem-solving, organizational, and time management skills, with a high level of attention to detail.
Effective technical writing and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with, or a strong understanding of, environmental modeling and the application of quantitative analyses to address environmental challenges involving contaminants in terrestrial, aquatic, and/or atmospheric systems.
Strong presentation skills, including experience with public speaking.
Proficiency in Python scripting; additional experience with geospatial programming languages such as SQL or Arcade is a plus.
Familiarity with statistics and statistical modeling software, such as R or SPSS, is a plus.
Research experience in a scientific field, including question development, methods documentation, and presentation of results; undergraduate thesis experience is a plus.

Physical Requirements

Ability to sit at a workstation and work on a computer for extended periods.
Ability to communicate effectively in-person and/or through electronic means.
Manual dexterity to use a computer mouse, keyboard, and other tools.
Visual acuity to read and interpret technical documents.

Additional Information

For this role, we are open to hybrid work schedules in our South Kingstown, Rhode Islandoffice, or remote work schedules within the eastern or central regional time zones of the United States.
This is a full-time position, typically 40 hours per week, with standard hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday. Additional hours may be required based on project needs.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
A collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 25,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

LinkedIn: @TetraTechCareers

X (Twitter): @TetraTechJobs

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

Please no phone calls or agencies.

Leidos is looking for a mission-driven Geospatial Analyst that will deliver GEOINT support to Counterintelligence (CI) operations. In this role, you will produce map-based analytic products that support customer critical mission functions, on-going IC partner relationships, and Request for Information (RFI)-driven analysis. Every product and activity you support will require a demonstrable counterintelligence nexus.

You will apply Activity-Based Intelligence (ABI) methodologies to fuse national and tactical ISR sources, providing timely, relevant, and accurate insights to IC partners.

Key Responsibilities

Produce map-based ABI analytic products in response to RFIs from IC partners.
Perform Line of Sight (LOS), proximity, and photo correlation analysis to support CI objectives.
Develop baseline imagery and mapping products supporting ongoing and emerging requirements.
Conduct multi-intelligence (multi-INT) fusion, with SIGINT focus, integrating national and tactical ISR sources.
Support and, where appropriate, co-author serialized intelligence reports internally within internal and with external IC partners.
Deliver capabilities briefings to potential new customers to expand mission partnerships.
Support sensitive activities originating from within and outside the agency, ensuring a counterintelligence nexus is maintained at all times.
Apply GEOINT tradecraft rigorously across diverse mission specifications, environments, and operational tempos.

ActiveTS/SCIclearance; willingness and ability to obtain aCI Polygraph.
5 years’ experience Demonstrating experience inGEOINT analysis, includingABImethodologies.
Proficiency with core analytic tools, including:

Analyst's Notebook / Renoir(or comparable link analysis tools)
Adobe Creative Suite

Experience inmulti-INT fusion, with a SIGINT focus,and integration of national and tactical ISR sources.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for RFI responses, briefings, and report co-authorship.

Experience withMotion GEOINT / FMVimagery analysis.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineering Lead
jobs.description:
Quantum Space is redefining mobility and maneuverability in space. Our high-mobility spacecraft platforms support national security, civil, and commercial missions with unmatched flexibility and propulsion capability. We build fast and iterate quickly.

Who We're Looking For

We are seeking a highly experienced Solution Engineering Lead to help shape the technical strategies behind some of the industry's most critical space missions.

This role serves as the technical architect for strategic pursuits, translating customer needs into innovative, executable mission solutions that position Quantum Space for long-term growth and competitive success. You will operate at the intersection of engineering, business development, capture, and executive leadership—developing mission architectures, evaluating technical approaches, establishing discriminators, and guiding solution strategies throughout the business development lifecycle. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in space systems engineering with strong strategic thinking and customer-focused solution development. You understand how to balance mission performance, technical risk, cost, schedule, and operational effectiveness while creating differentiated solutions that address complex customer challenges.

You are comfortable moving seamlessly between technical and strategic discussions, collaborating with engineers, capture managers, program leaders, executives, and government stakeholders to develop compelling mission concepts and winning technical approaches.

Whether supporting opportunities with the U.S. Space Force, Space Systems Command (SSC), Space Development Agency (SDA), AFRL, NASA, NRO, OSD, or other government customers, you recognize that exceptional solution engineering is a critical enabler of mission success, customer confidence, and company growth.

Where You'll Make an Impact

Solution Architecture & Technical Strategy

Lead technical solution development for strategic business pursuits across defense, intelligence, civil, and commercial space markets
Translate customer requirements into executable mission concepts, architectures, and technical approaches
Develop mission architectures, concepts of operation (CONOPS), and system-level solution strategies
Establish technical discriminators that clearly differentiate Quantum Space capabilities and offerings
Evaluate alternative approaches through technical trade studies and architecture assessments
Identify technical risks and develop mitigation strategies that improve solution credibility and execution confidence

Capture & Proposal Leadership

Partner with Capture Managers and Proposal Leaders to develop winning technical strategies
Provide technical leadership throughout the proposal lifecycle
Develop technical content, engineering approaches, and solution narratives for strategic pursuits
Participate in proposal reviews, color team reviews, and executive decision gates
Ensure proposed solutions are compliant, executable, innovative, and aligned with customer priorities

Customer Engagement & Mission Development

Support customer engagements, technical interchange meetings, and solution discussions
Present technical concepts, mission architectures, and solution strategies to government and commercial stakeholders
Help shape opportunities through early customer engagement and technical positioning activities
Maintain awareness of evolving mission needs, customer priorities, industry trends, and emerging technologies

Cross-Functional Leadership

Lead multidisciplinary technical teams during solution development activities
Collaborate across engineering, program management, business development, and executive leadership
Support multiple high-priority pursuits simultaneously in a fast-paced growth environment
Contribute to the development of repeatable solution engineering processes and best practices

What It Takes

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline
10+ years of experience developing space systems, mission architectures, or advanced aerospace solutions
Experience with spacecraft design, mission architecture development, satellite systems, communications systems, remote sensing, or national security space missions
Strong systems engineering background with demonstrated technical leadership experience
Experience conducting technical trade studies, requirements analysis, and solution development activities
Demonstrated ability to develop customer-focused technical solutions for complex government programs
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills
Ability to collaborate effectively across technical and non-technical organizations

Nice-to-Have Experience

Experience supporting opportunities with:
U.S. Space Force
Space Systems Command (SSC)
Space Development Agency (SDA)
Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL)
National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
National Reconnaissance Office (NRO)
Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD)

Prior experience supporting government space organizations, prime contractors, or advanced aerospace companies
Experience with satellite communications, space domain awareness, missile warning, ISR, remote sensing, or related mission areas
Familiarity with Department of Defense acquisition processes and proposal development activities
Advanced degree in a related technical discipline

What You’ll Get

Ownership – Lead the technical strategy behind high-priority space pursuits, developing mission architectures and solution concepts that shape Quantum Space's future
Innovation – Design forward-thinking mission solutions by combining systems engineering, customer insight, and emerging space technologies to solve complex national security, civil, and commercial challenges
Impact – Influence strategic business growth by developing differentiated technical approaches that strengthen customer confidence and position Quantum Space for long-term success
Growth – Partner with executive leadership, capture teams, and engineering experts while expanding your influence across business development, mission architecture, and strategic solution engineering
Compensation – Competitive salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous leave, HSA, 401(k) matching, and equity sharing

Location:
Rockville, MD or Hawthorne, CA

Base Salary:

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Quantum Space's total compensation package.

Additional Requirements

To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including ITAR, applicants must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual per 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Company Description
Luminia is a San Diego–based clean energy developer founded in 2019 that partners with not-for-profit clean electricity providers across California to deliver distributed solar and energy storage projects. The company focuses on strengthening grid resilience and creating long-term community benefits through a hyper-local approach that combines technical and financial expertise with strong community engagement and respect for local values. Luminia specializes in urban and commercial project siting to streamline permitting and interconnection, helping keep energy rates competitive while advancing clean energy goals. For commercial and industrial property owners, Luminia offers flexible financing and turnkey development solutions that unlock the value of rooftops and land, lower energy costs, and support sustainability objectives. With over 100 MW of distributed solar and storage in development, Luminia is committed to equitable, scalable projects that benefit the grid, the economy, and the communities it serves.

The Role

We're looking for a Project Coordinator to serve as the organizational backbone of our institutional partnership project pipeline. You'll track active projects from PPA execution through system energization, coordinating across internal engineering, external EPC partners, roofing contractors, tenants, and our institutional partner's team.

This isn't a role where you'll be making engineering or financial decisions. It's a role where you'll be the person who knows exactly where every project stands, who's responsible for the next step, and whether it's on track. When something slips, you'll be the first to notice and the first to flag it. When the engineering team is heads-down on technical work or pulled to another program, you'll be the voice keeping the institutional partnership projects moving.

Think of this as the connective tissue between our engineering team, our EPC partners, and our clients. The job is to make sure information flows, deadlines are tracked, and nothing gets deprioritized without a conscious decision.

What You'll Do

Project Tracking and Status Management

•        Maintain a comprehensive project tracker covering active projects from PPA execution through construction completion and permission to operate (PTO).
•       
Track key milestones: interconnection application submission and approval, permitting status, roof inspection and re-roof coordination, equipment procurement, construction scheduling, and PTO.
•       
Provide regular status updates to internal leadership and flag slippage or risks before they become problems.
•       
Ensure institutional partnership projects maintain priority and visibility when team resources are shared across programs.

Coordination and Communication

•        Coordinate between our engineering team, EPC partners, roofing contractors, and tenants on scheduling, access, and deliverables.
•       
Serve as the primary point of contact for routine project status inquiries from our institutional partner's team.
•       
Schedule and document project check-ins. Follow up on action items to ensure they're completed.
•       
Communicate with tenants on construction logistics, site access requirements, and timeline expectations.

Process Support

•        Support the interconnection application process by tracking submission deadlines, utility responses, and required documentation.
•       
Track permitting status across multiple jurisdictions and ensure EPC partners are meeting permitting timelines.
•       
Coordinate roof inspection scheduling with roofers and ensure re-roof work is completed ahead of solar installation.
•       
Assist with document management for construction-phase deliverables.

Qualifications

Required

•        1 to 3 years of experience in project coordination, project management, or a similar role. Solar, construction, or energy industry experience is a plus but not required.
•       
Exceptional organizational skills. You'll be tracking several projects simultaneously across multiple states and contractors.
•       
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. You'll be the go-between for internal teams, external partners, and clients.
•       
Proactive follow-up mindset. If something is due and hasn't been delivered, you follow up. If you haven't heard back, you follow up again. This is the core of the role.
•       
Proficiency with project tracking tools (Excel, Smartsheet, or similar).
•       
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
Preferred

•        Experience in solar, renewable energy, or commercial construction project management.
•       
Familiarity with utility interconnection processes and commercial building permitting.
•       
Experience working with institutional clients or large real estate portfolio owners.
•       
Comfort working in a small team environment where roles are flexible and ownership is expected.
What We Offer

•        A central role in one of the fastest-growing institutional solar programs in the country.
•       
Exposure to the full lifecycle of solar project development, from contract execution through energization.
•       
A small, collaborative team where your contributions are immediately visible and directly impact program success.
•       
Opportunity to grow into a project management role as the program scales.
•       
San Diego, CA location.

jobs.description:
Merch Project Production Coordinator

Location:
 New York, NY (hybrid — WFH is the default, office available but not required)
Type:
 Full-time contract
Compensation:
target ~$4,000/month, plus performance-based bonus potential (no benefits at this time, but working on adding in future — no 401k or health insurance)

The Role

Diskko produces merch for some of the world's biggest brands. This role owns that production from order to delivery. You are the person keeping every job on track — blanks, dye, print approvals, vendors, timelines — all at once, all the time.

This is not a 9-to-5, check-the-box job. Production doesn't pause for your schedule. Vendors need answers now. A color approval that sits for a day can blow a client's deadline. If you need a role with a predictable schedule, this isn't it. If you thrive on fast decisions, constant communication, and owning outcomes, this is exactly it.

What You'll Do
Order blanks
 — source and place orders with the right vendors, on the right timeline, for the right quantities
Place dye orders
 — manage custom dye jobs from spec to delivery
Approve colors and sizes
 — review and sign off on prints before they go into production, catching issues before they become problems
Manage multiple vendors simultaneously
 — juggle several active vendor relationships and production timelines at once, without dropping any of them
Communicate constantly and fast
 — you'll be in near-continuous contact with vendors, internal team, and sometimes clients. Slow or vague communication creates delays, and delays cost money
Troubleshoot in real time
 — when something goes sideways (and something always eventually does), you spot it early, figure out the fix, and communicate the issue and the plan clearly before it becomes a crisis
Call the shots
 — you'll be trusted to make production decisions on the fly, not wait around for sign-off on every call

What We Require
Extreme attention to detail.
 Nothing slips. Wrong sizes, wrong colors, missed dye windows — that's what this role exists to prevent
Organization under pressure.
 You're tracking multiple jobs, multiple vendors, multiple deadlines at once, and you never lose the thread
Fast, clear communicator.
 You respond quickly, you flag issues before you're asked, and you don't let things go quiet
A problem-solver, not just a task-doer.
 You see an issue coming and deal with it, rather than waiting for someone else to catch it
Comfortable with ownership.
 You're not looking for someone to tell you every next step — you take the job and run it

Experience

Merchandise production coordination experience is preferred, but not required. What matters more is that you're sharp, fast, detail-obsessed, results-driven, and genuinely want to grow with a small and scrappy team.

Growth

This role has a real path to Head of Project Management / Production. You'll also work directly with our sister company, Blanks By Thirteen, giving you exposure and growth across both sides of the business.

Bottom Line

If you want a calm, predictable role, this isn't the one. If you want to be the person who makes sure big brands' merchandise actually delivers, and you want a real shot at growing into a leadership role while you do it — apply.

Job Summary

In alignment with Brookdale’s Resident and Family Engagement philosophy, plans, coordinates and facilitates a calendar of person centered dementia friendly programs that meet specific needs of each and all residents within the dementia care community. Provides person centered programs while engaging residents in meaningful and purposeful dementia care programs within the Brookdale community enhancing their quality of life. Essential Functions

About Us

Augusta University is Georgia's innovation center for education and health care, training the next generation of innovators, leaders, and healthcare providers in classrooms and clinics on four campuses in Augusta and locations across the state. More than 12,000 students choose Augusta for educational opportunities at the center of Georgia's cybersecurity hub and experiential learning that blends arts and application, humanities, and the health sciences. Augusta is home to Georgia's only public academic health center, where groundbreaking research is creating a healthier, more prosperous Georgia, and world-class clinicians are bringing the medicine of tomorrow to patient care today. Our mission and values https://www.augusta.edu/about/mission.php make Augusta University an institution like no other.

Augusta University's distinct characteristics in education and research include real-world experiences and community engagement, as well as a culture of building community, corporate and government partnerships that address health, security, economic and societal concerns locally and across the state.

The University System of Georgia https://www.usg.edu/hr/orientation/welcome_to_the_board_of_regents_university_system_office is comprised of our 26 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found online at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.

Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found online at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653 .

Location

Augusta University

Our Health Sciences Campus: 1120 15th Street, Augusta, GA 30912

Our Summerville Campus: 2500 Walton Way, Augusta, GA 30904

College/Department Information

Training Future Leaders in Anesthesiology & Perioperative Patient Care. In our long history as an academic anesthesia department, The Medical College of Georgia¿s Department of Anesthesiology and Perioperative Medicine has established clerkships, a pain fellowship, and an anesthesiology critical care fellowship. A joint emergency medicine/anesthesiology critical care fellowship started in 2019 and we welcomed our first pediatric anesthesiology fellow in 2020. Our anesthesiology residency program provides comprehensive training in perioperative patient care, pain management and critical care medicine. We pride ourselves in training expert clinicians who are independent and confident when they graduate from our program. Our goal is to provide outstanding care to our patients by integrating education, evidence-based medicine, and research in daily patient care. Our board-certified faculty paired with the school¿s high-tech simulation lab provide an immersive learning experience. We believe in encouraging open feedback, new ideas, and innovations that lead to efficient clinical care and build strong relationships with our faculty and staff.

Job Summary

The Clerkship Coordinator provides comprehensive administrative and operational support for the Department of Anesthesiology and Perioperative Medicine's undergraduate medical education programs. This position coordinates all aspects of medical student clerkships, externships, visiting student rotations, observerships, and allied health student experiences, including scheduling, onboarding, evaluations, course management, and compliance activities.

The Coordinator serves as the primary liaison among students, faculty, regional campuses, and institutional offices to ensure a high-quality educational experience and efficient program operations. Responsibilities include managing course administration, maintaining student records and academic systems, coordinating orientations and access requirements, facilitating student advising and awards processes, and providing direct support to the Clerkship Director and departmental educational initiatives. The position also supports ongoing curriculum development, accreditation activities, and educational program expansion within the department.

Responsibilities

The duties include but are not limited to:

ENRICHMENT (M4) ROTATIONS EVERY 4 WEEKS: Pull all rosters from Banner. Verify all rosters with One45 rotation schedule. Send rotation contact/information to students. Collect student photos by rotation, distribute to faculty and front office staff. Locate student Asepsis Training dates. Prepare schedules for courses, distribute to faculty and front office staff. Monitor faculty responses to scheduled lectures, following up to reschedule as needed.

Success will be evident through higher technical win rates, reduced time to close, and increased adoption within key government accounts.

Proven success in pre-sales or solutions engineering, ideally supporting enterprise software or AI/ML platforms. This does not necessarily need to be at a software vendor, equivalent solution engineering tasks internally or as a consultant developer could work.

Track record of leading successful technical evaluations or pilots that resulted in multimillion-dollar enterprise or government software deals.
Experience working in complex, highly regulated IT environments, including hybrid or air-gapped systems.
Proficiency in Python, R, and modern data science / machine learning tools.
Familiarity with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), cloud platforms (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, GCP), and networking concepts.
Understanding of the end-to-end AI lifecycle, from experimentation to production.

At Dungarvin, we are dedicated to making a meaningful impact in the lives of individuals with diverse abilities. We provide essential support to those with intellectual and developmental disabilities, physical disabilities, autism, and mental health conditions - empowering them to thrive in their communities. Where barriers exist, we create pathways for inclusion and independence.

About our Adult Day Program:

Our Adult Day Program provides structured daytime services for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Individuals participate in skill-building, recreational, educational, and community-based activities that support independence, social connection, and personal goals. Staff work directly with individuals throughout the day, providing instruction, encouragement, personal care, behavioral support, and opportunities for meaningful participation.

The Role:

We are looking for an organized, confident, and proactive Program Coordinator for our Adult Day Program in Long Beach, CA.

The Program Coordinator (PC) is the lead Direct Support Professional (DSP) within the program. This is a hands-on working lead role, not a traditional administrative or supervisory position.

The PC works directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities throughout the day, providing personal care, instruction, skill development, and positive behavioral support. The goal is simple: keep individuals safe, engaged, supported, and moving toward greater independence.

The PC also helps keep the program running. This includes coordinating daily activities, adjusting schedules, supporting documentation, reinforcing expectations, and providing day-to-day guidance to DSP staff. The PC reports to the Program Director and leads through communication, consistency, and example, without formal supervisory authority.

Why You’ll Love This Role:

As a Residency Program Professional, you will provide essential management and oversight for graduate medical education (GME) programs, ensuring continued accreditation and operational excellence. “For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. As an OGI Field Technician (Travel), you’ll be responsible for performing hydrocarbon fugitive emission and /or leak detection of facilities in the Oil and Gas Industry in field. As well as work with industry leading technologies used to detect and measure methane gas emissions.

Atlas is a trusted leader in environmental and infrastructure consulting services; we provide services that enable communities to flourish and thrive. Job Description

Atlas is seeking a CMT Field Technician 1
to join our Construction Materials Testing team in Murfreesboro, Tennessee. In this role, you will perform field testing, inspection, and sampling activities that help ensure construction projects meet quality and safety standards.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys hands-on work, being outdoors, and contributing directly to projects that strengthen local communities.

Core Responsibilities

Perform field testing of concrete, soils, and other construction materials in accordance with project requirements.
Conduct field inspections and collect samples from active construction sites.
Accurately document test results and complete field reports.
Follow established safety procedures while working around construction activities and equipment.
Communicate effectively with project teams, supervisors, and clients regarding testing activities and results.
Travel to project sites throughout the region as needed

You’ll thrive here if you have

High school diploma or GED.

Strong communication and organizational skills.
Ability to read maps, follow directions, and interpret construction or engineering plans.
Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office and Excel.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions and stand or walk for extended periods.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and safely handle testing equipment and samples.
Valid driver's license and ability to meet company driving, background, and drug-screen requirements.

Description

Leidos is looking for a mission-driven Geospatial Analyst that will deliver GEOINT support to Counterintelligence (CI) operations. In this role, you will produce map-based analytic products that support customer critical mission functions, on-going IC partner relationships, and Request for Information (RFI)-driven analysis. Every product and activity you support will require a demonstrable counterintelligence nexus.

You will apply Activity-Based Intelligence (ABI) methodologies to fuse national and tactical ISR sources, providing timely, relevant, and accurate insights to IC partners.

Key Responsibilities

Produce map-based ABI analytic products in response to RFIs from IC partners.
Perform Line of Sight (LOS), proximity, and photo correlation analysis to support CI objectives.
Develop baseline imagery and mapping products supporting ongoing and emerging requirements.
Conduct multi-intelligence (multi-INT) fusion, with SIGINT focus, integrating national and tactical ISR sources.
Support and, where appropriate, co-author serialized intelligence reports internally within internal and with external IC partners.
Deliver capabilities briefings to potential new customers to expand mission partnerships.
Support sensitive activities originating from within and outside the agency, ensuring a counterintelligence nexus is maintained at all times.
Apply GEOINT tradecraft rigorously across diverse mission specifications, environments, and operational tempos.

Basic Qualifications

ActiveTS/SCIclearance; willingness and ability to obtain aCI Polygraph.
5 years’ experience Demonstrating experience inGEOINT analysis, includingABImethodologies.
Proficiency with core analytic tools, including:
ArcGIS Pro (ArcPro)
QT Modeler
RemoteView
Analyst's Notebook / Renoir(or comparable link analysis tools)
Adobe Creative Suite

Familiarity withIC proprietary toolscommonly used by ABI analysts.
Experience inmulti-INT fusion, with a SIGINT focus,and integration of national and tactical ISR sources.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for RFI responses, briefings, and report co-authorship.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience directly supportingCounterintelligenceorSpecial Programsmissions.
Experience withMotion GEOINT / FMVimagery analysis.
Familiarity with IC production standards and RFI workflows.
Experience deliveringcapabilities briefingsto new or prospective customers.

Understanding of theater operations and tactical ISR support.

new_jobs.title: Solutions Engineering Lead
new_jobs.description:
Quantum Space is redefining mobility and maneuverability in space. Our high-mobility spacecraft platforms support national security, civil, and commercial missions with unmatched flexibility and propulsion capability. We build fast and iterate quickly.

Who We're Looking For

We are seeking a highly experienced Solution Engineering Lead to help shape the technical strategies behind some of the industry's most critical space missions.

This role serves as the technical architect for strategic pursuits, translating customer needs into innovative, executable mission solutions that position Quantum Space for long-term growth and competitive success. You will operate at the intersection of engineering, business development, capture, and executive leadership—developing mission architectures, evaluating technical approaches, establishing discriminators, and guiding solution strategies throughout the business development lifecycle. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in space systems engineering with strong strategic thinking and customer-focused solution development. You understand how to balance mission performance, technical risk, cost, schedule, and operational effectiveness while creating differentiated solutions that address complex customer challenges.

You are comfortable moving seamlessly between technical and strategic discussions, collaborating with engineers, capture managers, program leaders, executives, and government stakeholders to develop compelling mission concepts and winning technical approaches.

Whether supporting opportunities with the U.S. Space Force, Space Systems Command (SSC), Space Development Agency (SDA), AFRL, NASA, NRO, OSD, or other government customers, you recognize that exceptional solution engineering is a critical enabler of mission success, customer confidence, and company growth.

Where You'll Make an Impact

Solution Architecture & Technical Strategy

Lead technical solution development for strategic business pursuits across defense, intelligence, civil, and commercial space markets
Translate customer requirements into executable mission concepts, architectures, and technical approaches
Develop mission architectures, concepts of operation (CONOPS), and system-level solution strategies
Establish technical discriminators that clearly differentiate Quantum Space capabilities and offerings
Evaluate alternative approaches through technical trade studies and architecture assessments
Identify technical risks and develop mitigation strategies that improve solution credibility and execution confidence

Capture & Proposal Leadership

Partner with Capture Managers and Proposal Leaders to develop winning technical strategies
Provide technical leadership throughout the proposal lifecycle
Develop technical content, engineering approaches, and solution narratives for strategic pursuits
Participate in proposal reviews, color team reviews, and executive decision gates
Ensure proposed solutions are compliant, executable, innovative, and aligned with customer priorities

Customer Engagement & Mission Development

Support customer engagements, technical interchange meetings, and solution discussions
Present technical concepts, mission architectures, and solution strategies to government and commercial stakeholders
Help shape opportunities through early customer engagement and technical positioning activities
Maintain awareness of evolving mission needs, customer priorities, industry trends, and emerging technologies

Cross-Functional Leadership

Lead multidisciplinary technical teams during solution development activities
Collaborate across engineering, program management, business development, and executive leadership
Support multiple high-priority pursuits simultaneously in a fast-paced growth environment
Contribute to the development of repeatable solution engineering processes and best practices

What It Takes

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline
10+ years of experience developing space systems, mission architectures, or advanced aerospace solutions
Experience with spacecraft design, mission architecture development, satellite systems, communications systems, remote sensing, or national security space missions
Strong systems engineering background with demonstrated technical leadership experience
Experience conducting technical trade studies, requirements analysis, and solution development activities
Demonstrated ability to develop customer-focused technical solutions for complex government programs
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills
Ability to collaborate effectively across technical and non-technical organizations

Nice-to-Have Experience

Experience supporting opportunities with:
U.S. Space Force
Space Systems Command (SSC)
Space Development Agency (SDA)
Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL)
National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
National Reconnaissance Office (NRO)
Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD)

Prior experience supporting government space organizations, prime contractors, or advanced aerospace companies
Experience with satellite communications, space domain awareness, missile warning, ISR, remote sensing, or related mission areas
Familiarity with Department of Defense acquisition processes and proposal development activities
Advanced degree in a related technical discipline

What You’ll Get

Ownership – Lead the technical strategy behind high-priority space pursuits, developing mission architectures and solution concepts that shape Quantum Space's future
Innovation – Design forward-thinking mission solutions by combining systems engineering, customer insight, and emerging space technologies to solve complex national security, civil, and commercial challenges
Impact – Influence strategic business growth by developing differentiated technical approaches that strengthen customer confidence and position Quantum Space for long-term success
Growth – Partner with executive leadership, capture teams, and engineering experts while expanding your influence across business development, mission architecture, and strategic solution engineering
Compensation – Competitive salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous leave, HSA, 401(k) matching, and equity sharing

Location:
Rockville, MD or Hawthorne, CA

Base Salary:

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Quantum Space's total compensation package.

Additional Requirements

To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including ITAR, applicants must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual per 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Apply now. Join us in building the next generation of spacecraft.

new_jobs.title: Merch Project Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Merch Project Production Coordinator

Location:
 New York, NY (hybrid — WFH is the default, office available but not required)
Type:
 Full-time contract
Compensation:
target ~$4,000/month, plus performance-based bonus potential (no benefits at this time, but working on adding in future — no 401k or health insurance)

The Role

Diskko produces merch for some of the world's biggest brands. This role owns that production from order to delivery. You are the person keeping every job on track — blanks, dye, print approvals, vendors, timelines — all at once, all the time.

This is not a 9-to-5, check-the-box job. Production doesn't pause for your schedule. Vendors need answers now. A color approval that sits for a day can blow a client's deadline. If you need a role with a predictable schedule, this isn't it. If you thrive on fast decisions, constant communication, and owning outcomes, this is exactly it.

What You'll Do
Order blanks
 — source and place orders with the right vendors, on the right timeline, for the right quantities
Place dye orders
 — manage custom dye jobs from spec to delivery
Approve colors and sizes
 — review and sign off on prints before they go into production, catching issues before they become problems
Manage multiple vendors simultaneously
 — juggle several active vendor relationships and production timelines at once, without dropping any of them
Communicate constantly and fast
 — you'll be in near-continuous contact with vendors, internal team, and sometimes clients. Slow or vague communication creates delays, and delays cost money
Troubleshoot in real time
 — when something goes sideways (and something always eventually does), you spot it early, figure out the fix, and communicate the issue and the plan clearly before it becomes a crisis
Call the shots
 — you'll be trusted to make production decisions on the fly, not wait around for sign-off on every call

What We Require
Extreme attention to detail.
 Nothing slips. Wrong sizes, wrong colors, missed dye windows — that's what this role exists to prevent
Organization under pressure.
 You're tracking multiple jobs, multiple vendors, multiple deadlines at once, and you never lose the thread
Fast, clear communicator.
 You respond quickly, you flag issues before you're asked, and you don't let things go quiet
A problem-solver, not just a task-doer.
 You see an issue coming and deal with it, rather than waiting for someone else to catch it
Comfortable with ownership.
 You're not looking for someone to tell you every next step — you take the job and run it

Experience

Merchandise production coordination experience is preferred, but not required. What matters more is that you're sharp, fast, detail-obsessed, results-driven, and genuinely want to grow with a small and scrappy team.

Growth

This role has a real path to Head of Project Management / Production. You'll also work directly with our sister company, Blanks By Thirteen, giving you exposure and growth across both sides of the business.

Bottom Line

If you want a calm, predictable role, this isn't the one. If you want to be the person who makes sure big brands' merchandise actually delivers, and you want a real shot at growing into a leadership role while you do it — apply.

Job Summary

The Markey Cancer Center is currently hiring a Research Coordinator
( Survivorship Research Program Manager)
to support a new research initiative. This position will provide essential administrative, research, and technical support to Initiative leadership to advance survivorship research at Markey. As described below, duties will include providing research proposal development support, communication management and partnership building, event and program planning, and administration and strategic planning. Pre-award research support will entail assisting with the development of human subjects and clinical trial documents for research proposals and developing protocols for regulatory submissions for Just-in-Time requests from funders. Communication management and partnership building will require serving as the front-line interface between Initiative leadership and varied stakeholders (e.g. investigators, clinicians, community partners, other units on campus). Event and program planning will require conception to post-event coordination and management for speaker series, research events, and other events led by the Initiative.

A successful candidate will have experience supporting or conducting human subjects research with cancer patients or other chronic or serious illness populations and knowledge of clinical trial requirements. In addition to being detail-oriented, self-motivated, and reliable, the successful candidate will exhibit maturity, customer service, excellent written and oral communication skills, an ability to prioritize and manage multiple deadlines, and good judgement. The successful candidate will have strong skills in MS software, remote meeting platforms, and online survey platforms (REDCap or Qualtrics).

This position is eligible for a Hybrid work arrangement.

IMPORTANT : Resumes and CVs cannot be substituted for a completed application. Incomplete applications could disqualify you from being considered for this position. .

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite programs, document and file management systems (e.g. SharePoint, One Drive, Microsoft Teams file repositories), project management/workflow tools for tracking tasks, timelines, and program plans, virtual meeting platforms, online survey administration systems; strong interpersonal skills; excellent written and oral communication

No

Master’s degree preferred, at least 3 years experience supporting human subjects research studies, with preference for clinically-focused research support, demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, attend to firm deadlines, and work with partners from a variety of disciplines.
